title: enrichVolcano
text: Related gene sets often reach significance together. GO:BP Reactome, one biological signal can light dozen overlapping terms. dedup_terms() flags one per cluster "redundant", plots hide redundant terms default (collapse = TRUE). row removed p-value changes: multiple-testing correction already covered every term, redundancy display decision. Within contrast database, significant terms walked smallest padj. term redundant gene set similar enough term already kept: similarity = "combined" (default, cutoff 0.375) EnrichmentMap coefficient (Merico et al. 2010; Reimand et al. 2019): mean Jaccard index overlap coefficient. overlap coefficient catches small set nested inside large one, Jaccard alone misses. similarity = "jaccard" (cutoff 0.5) shared genes genes either set. method = "collapse_pathways" different kind rule. calls fgsea::collapsePathways(), asks whether term still enriched genes significant term conditioned . new statistical test, needs ranking contrast tested , works ranked GSEA results, reported analysis. Call set.seed() first; permutes. published fgsea results carry flags computed upstream Jaccard rule. as_enrichment() keeps records object precomputed: Hallmark GO slim lose nothing built non-redundant. Deduplication matters large collections Reactome:
code: gene_sets <- split(msig$gene_symbol, msig$gs_name) x <- dedup_terms(x, gene_sets) x <- dedup_terms(x, gene_sets, similarity = "jaccard") x <- dedup_terms(x, gene_sets, method = "collapse_pathways", stats = list(Aging = ranks)) table(ex@results$dedup_status, ex@results$database, useNA = "ifany") #>             #>             GO Slim GO:BP Hallmark KEGG Reactome #>   kept           34   173       22   20      292 #>   redundant       0    79        0   35      261 #>   <NA>           74  3694      122   29      735 reactome <- load_gene_sets("Reactome") set.seed(1) aging <- run_enrichment(yvo, reactome, tests = "fgsea")$fgsea #> Up to 10 of 2103 ranked genes tie; fgsea orders tied genes arbitrarily. aging <- dedup_terms(aging, reactome$Reactome) plot_volcano_ring(yvo$da, aging, contrast = "Aging", title = "Aging, Reactome")

title: enrichVolcano
text: plot_scatter() plots every term’s score one contrast score another. answers two kinds question, set comparison. examples draw published fgsea results, ex; res$fgsea works way. default, comparison = "concordance", asks whether two conditions regulate pathways. Terms shaded top-right bottom-left quadrants move way .  comparison = "reversal" asks whether one condition undoes another. unshaded quadrants hold answer: pathway raised aging lowered training, reverse. reference line becomes y=−xy = -x.  term counts significant contrast padj term_threshold (0.05); colour says whether holds one contrast . Pathways judged false discovery rate alone. Scores combine effect size p, π\pi-value (Xiao et al. 2014), defined single proteins, gene sets. corner counts headline share use significant terms ; Spearman’s ρ\rho uses every plotted term, 95% Fieller interval (Fieller et al. 1957) correlation package (Makowski et al. 2020) installed. colour_by shape_by take per-term column, example colour_by = "database", databases, collapse label_min_size work ring.
code: plot_scatter(ex, "Training_Young", "Training_Old", databases = c("Hallmark", "GO Slim")) plot_scatter(ex, "Aging", "Training_Old",   comparison = "reversal", databases = c("Hallmark", "GO Slim") )

title: enrichVolcano
text: plot_theme() holds palette; plot arguments hold layout. arguments reach : magnitude: arc height encodes, "neg_log_padj" "size". arc_height_range: shortest tallest arc. arc_order: order arcs "padj" absolute score within half. x_scale, y_scale: compress volcano points crowd ring. label_mode, label_n, label_genes: proteins get text. labels: names chosen terms, c(HALLMARK_OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION = "OXPHOS"). show_counts, disc_colour: count badges tinted central disc.
code: plot_volcano_ring(yvo$da, res$fgsea,   contrast = "Training_Young",   theme = plot_theme(palette = "okabe"),   label_mode = "top_per_direction", label_n = 4 )

title: enrichVolcano
text: Every plot function returns one ggplot. write_plot() takes named list writes one PDF. Page 1 composite lettered , B, C list order. later page holds one panel full size, headed letter name. Fonts embedded. see composite screen, pass list patchwork::wrap_plots():  write_table() writes one enrichment object, whole list run_enrichment(), one CSV enrichment_test column:
code: panels <- list(   "Training, young" = plot_volcano_ring(yvo$da, res$fgsea, contrast = "Training_Young"),   "Training, old" = plot_volcano_ring(yvo$da, res$fgsea, contrast = "Training_Old"),   "Young against old" = plot_scatter(res$fgsea, "Training_Young", "Training_Old") ) write_plot(panels, "training.pdf", design = "AB\nCC", caption = "fgsea, Hallmark and GO slim") patchwork::wrap_plots(panels[1:2], ncol = 2) write_table(res, "yvo_enrichment.csv")
